# Brain (try4ever.com)

Brain is a study tool by try4ever that turns PDFs, DOCX, TXT and EPUB files into an interactive 3D knowledge map in the browser. Files are processed entirely on the user's device — no upload, no account database, no tracking. Free plan by application (apply once, study immediately with 21 nodes, more after review — no card), paid plan $19/mo. App lives at https://brain.try4ever.com.

## Pages

- [Brain – Turn PDFs & Notes Into a 3D Study Map](https://try4ever.com/): Turn PDFs and notes into a 3D map you can actually study from. Apply once, start immediately – no card, no countdown. Free plan by application; $19/mo for it all.
- [How Brain Works – From Upload to 3D Knowledge Map](https://try4ever.com/how/): Upload a PDF, DOCX, TXT or EPUB, watch it become a 3D graph of topics, quiz yourself, and track mastery from red to green. On-device processing, step by step.
- [Features – 3D Map, Mastery Tracking, Quizzes, Offline](https://try4ever.com/features/): A 3D knowledge map, color-coded mastery, quiz generation, offline mode and on-device file processing. Everything runs in your browser – no cloud, no tracking.

- [ADHD: Maps Beat Willpower](https://try4ever.com/blog/adhd-maps-beat-willpower/): When starting is the hard part and walls of text slide right off, a spatial map gives your attention a door. Visible structure, visible progress, no shame.
- [Changing Careers? Study Like a Pro](https://try4ever.com/blog/career-changers-map/): Retraining at 30, 40 or 50 means becoming a student again – usually with a mortgage and a calendar. You have more study skill than you think. Point it at a map.

- [Finals Week: From Cramming to Calm](https://try4ever.com/blog/finals-week-cram-to-calm/): All-nighters feel heroic and perform terribly. Finals week, rebuilt in four evenings: map it, quiz it, space it, sleep.
- [Developers: Docs Into a Map](https://try4ever.com/blog/developers-docs-to-map/): New stack on Monday, docs longer than the codebase. Feed the PDFs and EPUBs into a 3D map and see the architecture before the syntax.
- [IT Certs: Security+ to AWS, Mapped](https://try4ever.com/blog/it-certifications-map/): Ports, protocols, acronyms in ALL CAPS. Certification exams sound like soup because you're studying soup – domains and how they connect is the fix.
- [GRE & GMAT: Admissions Without Fog](https://try4ever.com/blog/gmat-gre-admissions-map/): Years out of school, studying after work, rusty quant and decayed vocabulary. The GRE and GMAT reward structure over stamina – here's the structure.
- [IB Diploma: Six Subjects, No Fog](https://try4ever.com/blog/ib-diploma-map/): Six subjects, TOK, the Extended Essay, CAS – the IB is coordination overload. Maps keep every thread visible at once.
- [JEE & NEET: Two Years, One Map](https://try4ever.com/blog/jee-neet-one-map/): Roughly two and a half million register for NEET-UG and over a million for JEE Main. The syllabus is two years deep. Structure is survival.
- [ASVAB: Map Your Way to the Job](https://try4ever.com/blog/asvab-line-scores-map/): Your ASVAB line scores decide which military jobs you can train for. Map the subtests that feed the score you actually need.
- [Parents: See Your Child's Real Progress](https://try4ever.com/blog/parents-track-progress/): 'I already studied, mom.' Meta-analyses link family involvement to real achievement gains – if you can see the studying. Now you can.
- [NREMT: Scenarios That Finally Click](https://try4ever.com/blog/nremt-paramedic-scenarios/): The NREMT asks about evolving patients, not isolated facts. If you studied protocols as lists, the scenarios felt like ambushes. Un-ambush them.
- [INBDE: Dental Boards, Mapped](https://try4ever.com/blog/dental-boards-inbde-map/): The INBDE replaced the two-part NBDE with one integrated exam. Integration is exactly what a map does – so study integrated.
- [NAPLEX: Hundreds of Drugs, One Map](https://try4ever.com/blog/naplex-pharmacology-map/): Pharmacology is taught as lists and tested as judgment. A map turns hundreds of drugs from alphabet soup into landscape.
- [NPTE: Map the Whole Body](https://try4ever.com/blog/npte-physical-therapy-map/): You learned the body in pieces – ortho here, neuro there, cardio somewhere else. The NPTE hands you whole patients. Maps reassemble them.
- [Teachers: Cut the Busywork, Keep the Craft](https://try4ever.com/blog/teachers-cut-prep-time/): Teachers work about 53 hours a week. AI should sharpen your craft, never replace it – here's a tool that takes the busywork, not the teaching.
- [PANCE: Ten Systems, One Map](https://try4ever.com/blog/pance-organ-systems-map/): The PANCE blueprint spreads hundreds of conditions across ten organ systems – but rotations taught them to you one ward at a time. Reconnect them.
- [Nursing School: Care Plans Without Panic](https://try4ever.com/blog/nursing-school-care-plans/): Clinicals by day, care plans by night, pharmacology somewhere in between. Nursing school is a systems problem – give it a map.
- [FE Exam: Engineering Formulas, Mapped](https://try4ever.com/blog/fe-exam-engineering-map/): The FE exam spans a dozen disciplines in one day. Thermodynamics, statics, ethics, econ – mapped, they finally behave like one subject.
- [Language Exams: Map Your Way to Fluency](https://try4ever.com/blog/language-exams-ielts-jlpt/): IELTS, TOEFL, JLPT, DELE – language exams test grammar in motion. Grammar patterns, vocab families and keigo all map beautifully.
- [GCSE & A-Levels: Revision You Can See](https://try4ever.com/blog/gcse-a-levels-revision/): Revision guides pile up, exam boards differ, and 'just revise' helps nobody. GCSE and A-Level students: make the revision visible.
- [AP, SAT, ACT: Big Exams, Small Panic](https://try4ever.com/blog/ap-sat-act-high-school/): AP exams, the SAT and the ACT reward students who can see structure. High schoolers: here's how to study smarter, not just longer.
- [CPA & CFA: Mountains of Material, Mapped](https://try4ever.com/blog/cpa-cfa-business-exams/): Accounting and finance exams bury you in standards and formulas. Maps turn FAR, AUD, REG and the CFA curriculum into visible structure.
- [Law Exams: See the Whole Case Map](https://try4ever.com/blog/law-school-lsat-bar-map/): Law school hides its structure inside hundreds of pages. IRAC, elements and exceptions become navigable when you can see the case map.
- [NCLEX Pharmacology That Finally Sticks](https://try4ever.com/blog/nclex-pharmacology-sticks/): 317,710 candidates sat the NCLEX last year – and a 73% pass rate means most walk in under-prepared. Pharmacology is where maps win.
- [MCAT Prep: Stop Rereading, Start Retrieving](https://try4ever.com/blog/mcat-stop-rereading/): More than 23,000 students matriculate into U.S. med schools each year – most of them beat the MCAT with retrieval, not rereading.
- [USMLE Step 1 Without the All-Nighter](https://try4ever.com/blog/usmle-step-1-map/): About 25,000 U.S. and Canadian students take Step 1 every year. The exam tests connections, not lists – study it that way.
- [Spaced Repetition vs 3D Maps: Use Both](https://try4ever.com/blog/spaced-repetition-vs-3d-maps/): Flashcard schedules and 3D maps solve different problems. The strongest study systems refuse to choose – here's how to combine them.
- [Watch Your Mastery Turn From Red to Green](https://try4ever.com/blog/red-to-green-mastery/): A progress bar you can see in 3D changes which topics you study next – and it changes how it feels to walk into an exam.
- [Why I Built Brain: Notes Into 3D Maps](https://try4ever.com/blog/why-i-built-brain/): Outlines hide the shape of what you're learning. I wanted to see it – so I built a tool that turns your own files into a 3D map.
- [The Chat That Changed How I Study](https://try4ever.com/blog/coffee-shop-conversation/): Two friends. One drowning in notes, one calm before finals. One question in a coffee shop that reveals the entire difference.
- [5 Study Hacks That Actually Survived Testing](https://try4ever.com/blog/weird-study-hacks/): Forget highlighters. Five unconventional study hacks that survived contact with real evidence – including one that involves walking in circles.
- [What a Learning Coach Told Me About Systems](https://try4ever.com/blog/learning-coach-interview/): A seasoned learning coach on why motivation is overrated, why systems win, and the three questions to ask before any study session.
- [Reading Five Times Is the Worst Way to Study](https://try4ever.com/blog/read-five-times-worst/): Rereading feels productive and delivers almost nothing. The 61%-vs-40% study every student should know – and the 20-minute fix.
- [Drowning in Lecture Notes? Here's the Fix](https://try4ever.com/blog/drowning-in-notes/): I used to hate studying. Then I learned to see my whole syllabus at once – and the stack of PDFs turned into a map I could walk.
- [Rote Memorization Fails. Your Brain Wants This](https://try4ever.com/blog/rote-memorization-inefficient/): Repeating facts until they hurt is the hardest way to learn. What research says works instead – and how to switch tonight.
- [A Poem for Every Tired Student](https://try4ever.com/blog/poetic-brain-stargazer/): Your hippocampus is a constellation of memories. A short poem for the nights when studying feels like falling – and a way back up.
- [Why a Map Beats a List for Memory](https://try4ever.com/blog/spatial-memory-power/): Your brain is a navigator, not a filing cabinet. Spatial memory turns lists you forget into places you know – here's the science and the shortcut.
